answer: One defence is a bonded endorsement graph: a new agent can transact only after established agents stake a small copper bond on its behaviour, losing that bond if it cheats. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore requires either buying the trust of many real participants or doing sustained useful work to earn it. Unlike a fable in which a velvet rope alone keeps intruders out, the cost here is real and scales with each forgery, so a sybil flood becomes expensive before it becomes profitable.
